16 OCTOBER 2026 · EVERYDAY EXPERIENCE

Start clearly.
Finish confidently.

A focused implementation of the three everyday journeys: improve a photo, prepare a batch, and retouch or censor an area. Existing editing engines and operation scope are preserved.

Implemented

  • The phone start screen gives Edit a photo clear priority, groups Resize and Convert as concise quick tasks, and separates creation workflows.
  • Retouch Photo opens an explicit single-photo target from its contextual menu. It uses the existing contextual selection route internally and preserves unrelated selection and batch inputs.
  • First-use Retouch and freeform Privacy guidance explains the next gesture near the tool, rather than requiring a trip to Help.
  • A photo/batch export finish card offers only successful outputs from that captured operation. Review & Share retains explicit manual approval; Mac offers Show in Finder. Failed new operations never offer old outputs as their result.
  • Optional sensitive checking is disclosed on demand in Review & Share; its capability limits and existing approval rules remain. Approval identifies the selected file count.
  • Empty workspaces offer a demo entry. The phone also offers Back to Start after cancelling an empty task, discovered during the live walkthrough.

Start and finish

Current native test captures. Completion screenshots follow real Image I/O processing and validated output creation, rather than fabricated processing results. Large-text layouts are scrollable.

Tools and batch scope

Verification and boundaries

  • Core: 117 tests passed.
  • Full iPhone and iPad targets: 230 tests each, one Photos-permission skip each, zero failures. Final UI-only refinement additionally checked by compact/accessibility native captures.
  • Focused Mac state and capture tests: 25 passed. The older unresolved long mixed native capture remains outside this focused run.
  • Both unsigned Release targets built. Two release-tool tests passed. Static preflight has zero failures and four submission blockers: public privacy/support URL verification and distribution signatures.
  • Regression coverage checks current-operation export results, total failure, Retouch single-photo routing, invalid multiple selection, cancellation, restored selection and stable batch inputs. Existing save/reopen, source preservation and safe export coverage remains.

A live iPhone Simulator walkthrough verified the new start screen, action-first editing entry and cancellation; it exposed the empty-workspace recovery gap that was then fixed. The final live walkthrough verified that Back to Start returns to the task choices and that Demo is visible in the empty workspace. Native captures are not a usability study. No claim that people love the app has been established. Testing with unfamiliar users, real-device Pencil/touch/keyboard, full VoiceOver traversal and performance checks remain.

Mac demo indexing still emits native Vision cache warnings. Simulator accessibility runtime warnings also occur. They are not declared resolved by these passing tests. Sources remain local and untouched; no signing, commit, push or publication.
